Marvila — Lisbon, Portugal

🟡 Local-source safety assessment · 24 areas reviewed individually Methodology →

Higher caution advised day Higher caution advised night

In detail

Marvila is the most heavily and repeatedly documented of the five for serious drug-related crime, largely centred on the Chelas public-housing area within it. Visão (3 Oct 2024) reported the conviction, to 19 years, of "Samir, rei do crack," leader of the so-called "grupo de Chelas"; Observador's special report described how PSP dismantled a group "controlled by terror" running one of Lisbon's busiest open-air drug points, earning about €3,000/day. Correio da Manhã separately reported Chelas youths threatening rivals with gun photos online, and JN reported an 11kg drug network dismantled in Chelas. PSP operations recur into 2025-2026: CNN Portugal covered a Marvila weapons/drugs cordon (Dec 2023), TVI/CNN reported four detained with drugs and guns seized in a Marvila bairro operation (21 Jan 2026), and TVI reported joint PSP searches of 12 homes across Olivais and Marvila (17 Dec 2025). Sources checked: Visão, 3 Oct 2024 – "Samir, rei do crack, líder do 'grupo de Chelas', foi condenado a 19 anos de prisão"; Observador (special) – "Grupo controlado pelo 'terror' e que rendia 3 mil euros por dia"; Correio da Manhã – "Grupo de jovens de Chelas ameaçam rivais de droga com fotografias de armas na 'net'"; Jornal de Notícias – "Policia desmantela rede de tráfico na zona de Chelas e apreende 11 quilos de droga"; CNN Portugal, 12 Dec 2023 – "Operação da PSP cerca Marvila à procura de armas e droga"; TVI Notícias / CNN Portugal, 21 Jan 2026 – "Quatro detidos, droga e armas apreendidas em operação da PSP em bairro de Lisboa" (Marvila); TVI Notícias, 17 Dec 2025 – "PSP faz buscas em 12 casas nos Olivais e em Marvila".

Frequently asked questions

Is Marvila safe?

Wandroz currently rates Marvila in Lisbon as an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Lisbon, both by day and after dark. This comes from a structured local-source assessment: an area-level review of credible local sources — local and national news, municipal and police-published material, and official surveys where they exist — consolidated across sources rather than taken from a single report. Lisbon publishes no comparable neighbourhood-level crime dataset; where a city does, Wandroz uses it instead.

Is Marvila safe at night?

At night, Marvila is rated as an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Lisbon. If you're unsure, it's worth checking recent local reviews for your specific street or block, since a neighbourhood-wide rating can't capture block-by-block variation.

Is Marvila a good area to stay in as a tourist?

Marvila's day rating (an area where the data suggests extra caution relative to other neighbourhoods in Lisbon) is the more relevant one for typical daytime tourist activity; check the night rating too if you'll be out late. The Booking.com link on this page searches Marvila itself.

Is there official crime data for Marvila?

Not an official government crime feed — Marvila's rating comes from Wandroz's own current local/national press and survey research for this specific area instead (see the note on this page for what was checked and the sources used). An absence of recent negative coverage is treated as inconclusive, not as proof the area is safe. If you live in or know Marvila well, you can suggest a correction using the link below.
